learn.title: Containers and serverless design
objectives: Choose between AKS, Azure Container Apps, Azure Container Instances, App Service and Azure Red Hat OpenShift by control, scale, cost and operational effort
Design AKS clusters: system and user node pools, autoscaling, network model, workload identity, private clusters and AKS Automatic
Design Azure Container Apps with Dapr, KEDA scale rules, scale to zero, revisions, jobs and workload profiles, and secure image supply with Azure Container Registry
Select an Azure Functions hosting plan (Flex Consumption, Premium, Dedicated, Container Apps) and apply Durable Functions patterns
Choose between Logic Apps Consumption and Standard and between code-first and low-code serverless designs
concepts: AKS system and user node pools
System node pools host critical system pods such as CoreDNS and metrics-server and must run Linux. User node pools host application pods and can use Windows, GPU or Spot VMs.
Cluster autoscaler vs HPA
The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler changes the number of pods. The cluster autoscaler adds or removes nodes when pods can't be scheduled or nodes are underused. KEDA adds event-driven pod scaling.
Azure CNI Overlay
Pods get IPs from a private overlay CIDR separate from the VNet, so large clusters use few VNet addresses. Flat Azure CNI gives pods VNet IPs that are directly routable from peered networks.
Microsoft Entra Workload ID

Federates a Kubernetes service account with a managed identity or app registration through the cluster OIDC issuer, so pods get tokens without stored secrets. It replaces the deprecated pod-managed identity.
AKS Automatic
An AKS mode where Azure manages system node pools, node autoprovisioning, upgrades, security defaults and deployment safeguards, while you keep full Kubernetes API access.
Azure Container Apps
Serverless container platform built on Kubernetes, KEDA, Dapr and Envoy. No direct Kubernetes API access. Supports scale to zero, revisions with traffic splitting, jobs and workload profiles.
Container Apps workload profiles

Consumption profiles are serverless and billed per replica use; Dedicated profiles reserve VM-sized nodes (general purpose, memory optimized, GPU) billed per instance. UDR egress needs a workload profiles environment.
Azure Container Instances
Runs a container group (one or more containers sharing lifecycle, network and storage) on demand with Hyper-V isolation. No built-in scaling, load balancing or certificates. Backs AKS virtual nodes.
Azure Container Registry
Private OCI registry. Premium tier adds geo-replication and private endpoints. ACR Tasks build and patch images in Azure, including on base image updates.
Functions Flex Consumption
The recommended serverless plan: Linux only, code-only (no containers), VNet integration, always-ready instances, per-function scaling and selectable instance memory. No deployment slots.
Durable Functions

Extension for stateful orchestrations in code. Patterns include chaining, fan-out/fan-in, async HTTP APIs, monitor, human interaction and aggregator (entities). Orchestrator code must be deterministic.
Logic Apps Consumption vs Standard

Consumption is multitenant, one workflow per resource, billed per execution. Standard is single-tenant on a hosting plan, holds many stateful or stateless workflows, supports VNet integration and private endpoints.
comparisons: Choose AKS when you need the Kubernetes API, custom operators or CRDs, Windows nodes or full cluster control. Choose Container Apps for microservices and jobs with minimal operations and scale to zero.
Container Apps adds scaling, revisions, ingress, certificates and Dapr. ACI is a low-level building block for single run-once or simple isolated container groups.
App Service suits web apps and APIs that need deployment slots, Windows containers or App Service features. Container Apps suits event-driven microservices that scale to zero.
Flex Consumption vs Premium vs Dedicated

Flex: serverless pay per use with VNet and optional always-ready instances. Premium: always-warm instances, Windows or Linux containers, slots. Dedicated: fixed App Service plan cost, reuse existing plans, ASE isolation.
Durable Functions is code-first orchestration for developers. Logic Apps is a low-code designer with hundreds of connectors for integration workflows.

Consumption for low or intermittent volume and simple setup. Standard for VNet access, many workflows per app, stateless high-throughput workflows, local development and predictable cost at high volume.
traps: Azure Container Apps can't run Windows containers and doesn't expose the Kubernetes API; pick AKS when either is required.
Flex Consumption doesn't support custom containers, Windows or deployment slots. Premium or Container Apps hosting may be required.
HTTP-triggered functions must respond within 230 seconds regardless of plan timeout; use the Durable Functions async HTTP pattern for long work.
Geo-replication and private endpoints in Azure Container Registry require the Premium tier.
A container app with ingress disabled and no scale rule or minimum replica can scale to zero and never start again.
The legacy Consumption plan is not the default choice for new function apps; Linux Consumption is retiring, so use Flex Consumption.
revision: Need the Kubernetes API or Windows containers with orchestration: AKS. Want Kubernetes-style microservices without managing clusters: Container Apps.
Simple run-once or burst containers: ACI, or AKS virtual nodes for bursting from a cluster.
Use workload identity for pod access to Azure resources and private clusters to keep the API server off the internet.
Container Apps: KEDA rules for event scaling, multiple revision mode for traffic splitting, jobs for run-to-completion tasks, Dedicated profiles for large or memory-heavy replicas.
New serverless functions: Flex Consumption. Windows, containers, slots or always-warm: Premium. Fixed cost or ASE: Dedicated. Custom image or GPU: Container Apps hosting.
Durable patterns: chaining, fan-out/fan-in, async HTTP, monitor, human interaction, aggregator.
Logic Apps Standard replaces ISE for single-tenant, network-isolated integration workflows.

questions.q: A team needs to run a single containerized script once a week for about 20 minutes. It needs no load balancing, scaling or ingress, and the team wants to pay only while it runs with no platform to manage. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure App Service for Containers on a Basic plan
Azure Container Instances with the restart policy set to Never
An AKS cluster with a single user node pool
An Azure VM with Docker that is started by a schedule

questions.q: Which Azure Container Registry service tier is required to enable geo-replication of a registry to other Azure regions?
opts: Basic
Any tier, as geo-replication is a free add-on
Premium
Standard

questions.q: In Azure Kubernetes Service, what is the main purpose of a system node pool?
opts: To provide Spot capacity for interruptible application pods
To host critical system pods such as CoreDNS and metrics-server
To run the managed Kubernetes control plane components
To host only Windows Server application containers
questions.e: Every AKS Standard cluster needs at least one Linux system node pool. Application workloads should go on user node pools.

questions.q: A platform team must deploy a third-party Kubernetes operator that installs custom resource definitions and needs direct access to the Kubernetes API server. Which service should you recommend?
opts: Azure Container Instances
Azure Container Apps
Azure App Service for Containers
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
questions.e: Container Apps is built on Kubernetes but doesn't expose the Kubernetes APIs. Operators and CRDs need AKS.

questions.q: A company has standardized on Red Hat OpenShift on-premises and wants a jointly supported managed OpenShift service in Azure with the same tooling. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Container Apps with Dapr enabled
Azure Container Instances in a virtual network
Azure Red Hat OpenShift
AKS Automatic with the application routing add-on

questions.q: In Azure Container Instances, what is a container group?
opts: A set of container images that are replicated between registries
A scale set of identical containers behind a built-in load balancer
A logical folder used to apply RBAC to many container instances
A set of containers scheduled on the same host that share a lifecycle, network and storage volumes

questions.q: Which change to an Azure Container Apps app creates a new revision?
opts: Adding a new secret to the app configuration
Switching the app between single and multiple revision mode
Updating the container image tag in the app template
Changing the traffic weights between existing revisions
questions.e: Revision-scope changes (template: image, environment variables, scale rules) create a revision. Application-scope changes such as secrets, ingress and revision mode don't.

questions.q: A web app runs as a custom container on Azure App Service. The team wants to warm up a new version and move it to production without downtime, with quick rollback. What should you recommend?
opts: Deploy a second App Service plan and change the DNS record
Restart the app after pushing a new image to the same tag
Scale out to two instances and deploy to one at a time manually
Deploy to a staging deployment slot and swap it with production

questions.q: An AKS workload scales pods with the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, but new pods stay Pending because nodes are full. Which feature adds nodes automatically in this situation?
opts: A second Horizontal Pod Autoscaler with a lower target
Pod disruption budgets on the deployment
The cluster autoscaler on the user node pool
The Vertical Pod Autoscaler in recommendation mode

questions.q: Security policy requires application images to be rebuilt automatically whenever their base OS image is patched, without running build servers. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Container Registry Tasks with a base image update trigger
Azure Container Registry geo-replication to a second region
An AKS CronJob that pulls and re-tags images every night
Microsoft Defender for Containers vulnerability assessment only

questions.q: A company plans a large AKS cluster but has only a small address range left in its hub-and-spoke VNet design. Pods don't need to be addressed directly from other networks. Which network model should you recommend?
opts: Host networking for every pod on the nodes
Azure CNI with a dynamic pod subnet sized for all pods
Azure CNI Overlay
Azure CNI with pods assigned IPs from the node subnet
questions.e: Overlay assigns pod IPs from a private CIDR that isn't part of the VNet, so only nodes consume VNet addresses.

questions.q: An AKS cluster runs general web services. A new inference service needs GPUs, and other pods must not be scheduled on the expensive GPU nodes. What should you recommend?
opts: Add a GPU user node pool with a taint, and give only the inference pods a matching toleration
Resize the system node pool to a GPU VM size
Create a second AKS cluster for every GPU workload
Add GPU VMs to the system node pool and set pod priority

questions.q: Pods in an AKS cluster must read secrets from Azure Key Vault. The security team forbids storing client secrets or certificates in the cluster. What should you recommend?
opts: The Key Vault access keys mounted as environment variables
Microsoft Entra Workload ID with a federated credential on a managed identity
Microsoft Entra pod-managed identity with the NMI daemon
A service principal secret stored in a Kubernetes secret
questions.e: Workload ID federates a Kubernetes service account with an Entra identity through the cluster OIDC issuer, so no secret is stored.

questions.q: Compliance requires that the AKS API server has no public endpoint and is reachable only from the corporate network over ExpressRoute. What should you recommend?
opts: Deploy AKS as a private cluster
Use a network security group on the node subnet
Put an Application Gateway in front of the API server
Enable authorized IP ranges on the public API server

questions.q: An AKS cluster sees short, unpredictable spikes of Linux pods. The team wants extra capacity in seconds without waiting for new VMs and without paying for idle nodes. What should you recommend?
opts: Raise the minimum node count of the cluster autoscaler
Enable virtual nodes so pods burst to Azure Container Instances
Add a Windows user node pool for overflow pods
Switch the system node pool to larger VM sizes
questions.e: Virtual nodes schedule pods onto Azure Container Instances, giving fast capacity billed per second without adding VMs.

questions.q: A team new to Kubernetes must run containers with full Kubernetes API access, but wants Azure to manage node provisioning, upgrades and security defaults to minimise operational effort. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Container Apps on a Consumption profile
AKS Standard on the Free tier
Azure Container Instances with container groups
AKS Automatic
questions.e: AKS Automatic keeps full Kubernetes API access while Azure manages system nodes, node autoprovisioning, upgrades and safeguards.

questions.q: Developers are building microservices on Azure Container Apps. They want service-to-service calls with built-in retries and mTLS, plus pub/sub, without writing that plumbing for each SDK. What should you recommend?
opts: Use Azure Container Instances sidecars for each service
Deploy an Istio service mesh in the environment
Enable managed Dapr on the container apps
Expose each app with external ingress and call public URLs

questions.q: A worker container on Azure Container Apps processes messages from an Azure Service Bus queue. It must scale out with queue depth and cost nothing when the queue is empty. What should you configure?
opts: A custom Service Bus scale rule with minimum replicas set to 0
Manual scaling with a fixed replica count of 10
An HTTP scale rule with minimum replicas set to 1
A CPU scale rule with minimum replicas set to 3

questions.q: A team wants to send 10 percent of production traffic to a new version of a container app and increase it gradually. What should you configure in Azure Container Apps?
opts: A scheduled job that switches the image tag hourly
Single revision mode with two replicas of the new image
A second environment and DNS weighted round robin
Multiple revision mode with traffic weights between revisions
questions.e: Single revision mode keeps only one active revision. Traffic splitting needs multiple revision mode.

questions.q: A containerized data clean-up task must run every night at 02:00 and stop when finished. The rest of the solution already runs in an Azure Container Apps environment. What should you recommend?
opts: A Container Apps job with a schedule (cron) trigger
An AKS cluster running a Kubernetes CronJob
A container app with an HTTP scale rule called by a timer
A container app with minimum replicas set to 1

questions.q: Each message in a queue triggers a long video-encoding task that must run to completion in its own container execution. Which Azure Container Apps option fits best?
opts: A container app with a TCP scale rule
A manually triggered Container Apps job
An event-driven Container Apps job
A container app in single revision mode

questions.q: A container app needs 32 GiB of memory per replica for an in-memory model and runs steadily all day. What should you recommend in Azure Container Apps?
opts: A Dedicated memory-optimized workload profile
A Container Apps job with a larger timeout
The default Consumption workload profile
A Consumption profile with more replicas of 2 GiB each
questions.e: Consumption profile replicas are limited to small sizes. Dedicated E-series profiles provide much larger memory per node.

questions.q: A company has several .NET Framework services in Windows containers that need orchestration, rolling updates and service discovery. What should you recommend?
opts: AKS with a Windows Server system node pool only
AKS with a Windows Server user node pool
Azure Container Apps with a Dedicated profile
Azure Functions Flex Consumption

questions.q: A workload must run as Windows containers. Which platform should you NOT recommend?
opts: Azure Container Apps
Azure Container Instances
Azure Kubernetes Service
Azure App Service

questions.q: A single containerized web API must have staging deployment slots with swap, App Service authentication and autoscale. It never needs to scale to zero. What should you recommend?
opts: AKS with the application routing add-on
Azure Container Instances with a public IP
Azure App Service for Containers on a Premium plan
Azure Container Apps on a Consumption profile

questions.q: A company runs eight low-traffic containerized web apps, each on its own App Service plan. CPU usage on every plan stays below 5 percent. How should you minimise cost?
opts: Enable autoscale on each plan with a maximum of five instances
Move each app to a separate App Service Environment
Add a deployment slot to each app
Consolidate the apps onto one App Service plan sized for their combined load

questions.q: An AKS cluster runs stateless, fault-tolerant worker pods that can be interrupted and restarted. How should you reduce compute cost for these pods?
opts: Run them on a Spot user node pool with tolerations
Disable the cluster autoscaler and overprovision nodes
Move them to the system node pool to share capacity
Run them on a Spot system node pool

questions.q: AKS clusters pull public base images from Docker Hub and sometimes hit Docker Hub pull rate limits. Images must be served from the company's own Azure Container Registry with minimal pipeline changes. What should you recommend?
opts: Switch the node pools to Azure Container Instances virtual nodes
Configure an artifact cache rule in Azure Container Registry for the Docker Hub repositories and pull through the registry
Enable geo-replication on the registry
Increase the AKS node count so pulls are spread across more nodes
questions.e: Artifact cache lets a registry pull and cache images from upstream public registries, so clusters pull from your registry instead of Docker Hub.

questions.q: Build agents and AKS nodes must reach Azure Container Registry only over private IP addresses, with public network access disabled. What should you recommend?
opts: The Premium tier with a private endpoint
The Basic tier with a firewall rule for the VNet
The Standard tier with a service endpoint
The Standard tier with geo-replication
questions.e: Private endpoints for Azure Container Registry require the Premium tier.

questions.q: A short-lived container task in Azure Container Instances must connect to a database that accepts traffic only from a private subnet. What should you recommend?
opts: Run the task from an Azure App Service Basic plan
Use a geo-replicated Azure Container Registry
Deploy the container group into a delegated subnet of the virtual network
Give the container group a public IP and allow it on the database

questions.q: A task in Azure Container Instances needs a log-shipping helper that reads the main container's log files and shares its lifecycle. What should you recommend?
opts: Create a separate container group and connect it with a public IP
Run the helper on an AKS virtual node
Deploy the helper as an Azure Function on a timer
Add the helper as a second container in the same container group with a shared volume

questions.q: Evaluate these statements about Azure Container Apps. 1: An app can scale to zero replicas. 2: Administrators can run kubectl against the underlying cluster. 3: Dapr can be enabled as a managed feature. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3
Statements 1 and 2 only

questions.q: Development AKS clusters are used only during business hours. How should you reduce their cost with the least effort?
opts: Delete the system node pool every evening
Stop the clusters outside business hours and start them each morning
Switch the clusters to the Premium tier
Scale the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler maximum to one

questions.q: A production AKS Standard cluster needs a financially backed uptime SLA for the Kubernetes API server, while long-term support isn't needed. Which tier should you recommend at the lowest cost?
opts: Premium tier
Free tier
Free tier with availability zones
Standard tier

questions.q: Production and test container apps must not share a virtual network or Log Analytics workspace. How should you design Azure Container Apps?
opts: Put both in one environment with separate workload profiles
Create separate Container Apps environments for production and test
Put both in one environment with different revision labels
Use one environment and separate ingress ports
questions.e: Apps in the same environment share the same virtual network and logging destination, so the environment is the isolation boundary.

questions.q: AKS clusters in three regions pull the same images. Pulls must stay in-region for low latency, images must be managed in one place, and traffic must stay private. What should you recommend?
opts: One Standard registry in the primary region with service endpoints
Three Standard registries kept in sync by a nightly import script
One Premium registry in one region fronted by Azure Front Door
One Premium registry geo-replicated to all three regions, with private endpoints in each region
questions.e: Geo-replication gives one registry name with regional replicas, so each cluster pulls from its nearest replica.

questions.q: A background container app has ingress disabled, no scale rules and default replica settings. After deployment it never processes any work. What is the most likely cause and fix?
opts: Single revision mode stops idle apps; switch to multiple revision mode
It scaled to zero with nothing to wake it; add an event scale rule or set minimum replicas to 1
Ingress must be enabled for any container to start; enable external ingress
The default profile can't run background apps; add a Dedicated profile
questions.e: Without ingress, a custom scale rule or minReplicas of 1 or more, the default rule lets the app scale to zero and nothing can start it again.

questions.q: A team has 30 microservices. They use Helm charts with custom resources from a database operator and want GitOps on cluster state. Operations staff are experienced with Kubernetes. Which platform best fits?
opts: Azure Kubernetes Service
Azure App Service with sidecars
Azure Container Instances
Azure Container Apps

questions.q: A startup builds 12 Linux microservices. Traffic is bursty and some services are idle for hours. The team has no Kubernetes experience, wants scale to zero and doesn't need the Kubernetes API. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Container Instances with one group per service
AKS Standard with the cluster autoscaler
Azure Container Apps on the Consumption profile
Azure App Service with one plan per service

questions.q: After an AKS cluster is made private, administrators working from the internet can no longer run kubectl, and no VPN exists. You must allow occasional admin commands without exposing the API server publicly. What should you recommend?
opts: Expose the API server through a public load balancer service
Add the administrators' IPs to authorized IP ranges
Re-enable the public FQDN and restrict it with an NSG
Use the AKS run command (az aks command invoke) or a jump box in a connected VNet

questions.q: A proposed AKS design uses Microsoft Entra pod-managed identity so pods can access Azure Storage. What should you recommend instead?
opts: Storage account keys, because managed identities don't work with AKS
Microsoft Entra Workload ID, because pod-managed identity is deprecated
A shared service principal secret in a ConfigMap
The kubelet identity for every pod in the cluster

questions.q: Evaluate these statements about AKS Automatic. 1: AKS manages the system node pools for you. 2: You can't use the Kubernetes API directly. 3: Deployment safeguards enforce Kubernetes best practices through Azure Policy. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3
Statement 3 only

questions.q: An image-generation API needs GPUs but receives requests only a few times a day. The company wants GPU acceleration while paying nothing when idle and avoiding cluster management. What should you recommend?
opts: A Dedicated GPU workload profile with one instance always on
An AKS GPU node pool with a minimum of one node
Azure Container Apps with a serverless GPU Consumption profile and scale to zero
An NC-series VM that is started manually

questions.t: ACI vs ACA for web app
questions.q: A long-running containerized HTTPS API needs autoscaling, managed certificates for a custom domain and rolling revisions. Which service should you NOT recommend?
opts: Azure Container Apps
Azure Container Instances
Azure Kubernetes Service
Azure App Service for Containers
questions.e: ACI has no built-in scaling, load balancing or certificate management; you would have to build them yourself.

questions.q: Testers must reach a new container app revision through its own stable URL before it receives any production traffic. What should you configure in Azure Container Apps?
opts: A separate environment with internal ingress
Single revision mode with a second replica
Multiple revision mode, 0 percent traffic to the new revision, and a revision label
A Container Apps job triggered by the testers

questions.q: A Linux custom container on Azure App Service must send telemetry through an OpenTelemetry collector that runs next to the app container. The team wants to stay on App Service. What should you recommend?
opts: Add the collector as a sidecar container on the web app
Run the collector in a separate App Service plan
Install the collector inside a deployment slot
Move the app to Azure Container Instances

questions.q: An AKS cluster uses Azure CNI Overlay. An on-premises system must call a service in the cluster over ExpressRoute, but calls to pod IPs fail. What should you recommend without redeploying the cluster?
opts: Change the pods to use host networking
Add a route to the pod CIDR on the on-premises router
Enable authorized IP ranges for the on-premises network
Expose the service through an internal load balancer with a VNet IP
questions.e: Overlay pod IPs aren't routable outside the cluster. Use a Kubernetes service with an internal load balancer for inbound traffic.

questions.q: Container apps must be reachable only from a private network, and all outbound traffic must be forced through Azure Firewall with user-defined routes. What should you recommend?
opts: A Consumption-only environment with external ingress
A workload profiles environment in a custom VNet with internal ingress and a UDR to the firewall
A workload profiles environment in a managed VNet with public ingress
Azure Container Instances with a public IP and NSG
questions.e: User-defined routes are available only in workload profiles environments deployed into your own VNet.

questions.q: An AI assistant generates Python code that must run in strongly isolated, short-lived sandboxes with fast startup, managed as a pool. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Functions Premium plan with slots
An AKS namespace per user with network policies
Azure App Service with one app per user
Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions

questions.q: A manufacturer must run containers in factories with intermittent internet and in Azure, using the same Kubernetes tooling and Azure-based governance. What should you recommend?
opts: AKS on Azure Local in the factories and AKS in Azure, managed through Azure Arc
Azure Container Apps in each factory
Azure Red Hat OpenShift on factory hardware managed by Microsoft
Azure Container Instances deployed to the factories

questions.q: A team is creating a new serverless Azure Functions app and wants pay-per-use billing and fast event-driven scale. Which hosting plan does Microsoft recommend for new serverless function apps?
opts: Dedicated (App Service) plan
Premium plan
Flex Consumption plan
Consumption plan
questions.e: The Consumption plan is now legacy. Microsoft recommends Flex Consumption for new serverless apps.

questions.q: Which Durable Functions pattern runs many activity functions in parallel and then waits for all of them to finish to aggregate the results?
opts: Function chaining
Fan-out/fan-in
Human interaction
Monitor

questions.q: An order process must validate, then charge, then ship, where each step uses the output of the previous one and runs in a fixed order. Which Durable Functions pattern fits?
opts: Fan-out/fan-in
Async HTTP APIs
Function chaining
Aggregator (durable entities)

questions.q: A simple workflow posts a Teams message when a SharePoint list item is added, a few times a day. It needs no virtual network access. Which option minimises cost and setup?
opts: Logic Apps Consumption
Azure Functions on a Dedicated plan
Logic Apps Standard in an App Service Environment v3
Logic Apps Standard on a Workflow Standard plan

questions.q: Regardless of the function timeout setting, what is the maximum time an HTTP-triggered Azure function can take to respond to a request?
opts: 60 minutes
5 minutes
230 seconds
10 minutes
questions.e: This limit comes from the Azure Load Balancer idle timeout. Use the Durable Functions async HTTP pattern for longer work.

questions.q: True or false: the Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan can host function apps on Windows.
opts: True. It supports both Windows and Linux
False. Flex Consumption supports only Linux
True, but only for .NET apps
False. It supports only Windows containers

questions.q: A Windows-based function app must respond with no cold-start delay after idle periods and connect to a virtual network. Which plan should you recommend?
opts: Dedicated plan without Always On
Flex Consumption plan
Premium plan with always-ready instances
Consumption plan

questions.q: Functions run on a Dedicated (App Service) plan. Which setting must be enabled so that non-HTTP triggers keep running and long executions are supported?
opts: Client certificates
Always On
Auto swap

questions.q: A team wants to group 15 related workflows in a single Logic Apps resource so they deploy and share configuration together. Which option supports this?

Power Automate cloud flows
Logic Apps Standard
Logic Apps Consumption with an integration account

questions.q: A team wants to use the Azure Functions programming model in a custom Linux container and run it alongside other microservices without managing Kubernetes. Which hosting option should you recommend?

questions.q: A function uses Windows-only PowerShell modules, needs VNet integration and must never wait for a cold start. Which plan should you recommend?

questions.q: A company has an underused App Service plan running web apps and wants to add a few function apps with fully predictable billing. What should you recommend?

questions.q: Clients call an HTTP API that starts a report taking up to 20 minutes. Clients need a status URL to poll for the result. What should you recommend?

questions.q: A Flex Consumption function processes large files and runs out of memory on the default instance size. What should you recommend first?
opts: Add deployment slots to spread the load
Set the instance memory size to 4,096 MB
Increase the function timeout
Move to the Consumption plan for more memory
questions.e: Flex Consumption lets you choose 512 MB, 2,048 MB or 4,096 MB instances.

questions.q: A design places a function app on Flex Consumption and relies on deployment slot swaps for zero-downtime releases. What is wrong with the design?
opts: Slots work only with Windows containers
Slots are supported but can't be swapped automatically
Slots require a Dedicated plan in an ASE
Flex Consumption doesn't support deployment slots; use the Premium plan if slots are required

questions.q: A function app must accept inbound traffic only through a private endpoint. Which hosting option should you NOT recommend?
opts: Dedicated plan
Flex Consumption plan
Azure Container Apps hosting
Premium plan
questions.e: Functions on Container Apps don't support inbound private endpoints; ingress is managed by the Container Apps environment.

questions.q: An event-driven inference function needs GPU compute and should use the Functions triggers and bindings model. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Functions hosted on Azure Container Apps with a GPU workload profile
Logic Apps Standard with a custom connector
Azure Functions Premium plan with the largest instance
Azure Functions Flex Consumption with 4,096 MB instances

questions.q: A company has many Python function apps on the Linux Consumption plan and wants new language versions and features. What should you recommend?
opts: Keep them and enable always-ready instances
Migrate the apps to the Flex Consumption plan
Convert them to Logic Apps Consumption
Move them to the Windows Consumption plan

questions.q: True or false: an Azure Container Apps app on the Consumption profile incurs no usage charges while it is scaled to zero replicas.
opts: True, but only for apps without ingress
False. Scale to zero is supported only on Dedicated profiles
False. Idle replicas are always billed at the full rate
True. Usage charges stop when the app scales to zero

questions.q: Regulations require some integration workflows to run on-premises, close to local systems, while being managed from Azure. What should you recommend?
opts: Logic Apps Standard with the hybrid deployment model on Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes
Power Automate desktop flows
An integration service environment in the datacenter
Logic Apps Consumption with an on-premises data gateway

questions.q: A team has ten small function apps that each need VNet access and warm instances. How should you minimise cost while keeping event-driven scale?
opts: Create a Flex Consumption plan for each app with always-ready instances
Host each app in its own App Service Environment
Create a separate Premium plan for each app
Host all ten apps on one shared Premium plan

questions.q: In Durable Functions, where should code that calls an external API or reads from a database be placed?
opts: In an activity function called by the orchestrator
In the orchestration client function only
In a durable timer callback
Directly in the orchestrator function body

questions.q: A company used a Logic Apps integration service environment (ISE) for network isolation. What should it use for new isolated integration workflows?
opts: Logic Apps Consumption with an integration account
Logic Apps Standard
Azure Functions Consumption plan
A new integration service environment
questions.e: Integration service environments are retired. Logic Apps Standard provides single-tenant hosting with VNet integration.

questions.q: A function app runs almost continuously with a very high number of small executions, giving a large execution-count bill on a pay-per-execution plan. Which plan offers more predictable cost?
opts: Consumption plan on Windows
Azure Container Apps with minimum replicas set to zero
Flex Consumption plan with smaller instances
Premium plan

questions.q: A queue-triggered function on the legacy Consumption plan hits its maximum execution time. It must keep serverless pay-per-use billing. What should you recommend?
opts: Move to the Flex Consumption plan and raise the function timeout
Set functionTimeout above 10 minutes on the Consumption plan
Move to a Dedicated plan without Always On
Split the function into an HTTP trigger
questions.e: The Consumption plan caps execution at 10 minutes. Flex Consumption has no enforced maximum, with a grace period on scale-in.

questions.q: An event-driven Python API must: reach private resources in a VNet, scale to zero, deploy code without containers, run on Linux and minimise cost. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Functions on Container Apps with minimum replicas set to zero
Azure Functions Flex Consumption with VNet integration
Azure Functions Consumption plan on Linux
Azure Functions Premium plan with VNet integration

questions.q: A Durable Functions orchestrator reads the current time with the system clock and generates GUIDs directly. Orchestrations behave inconsistently after restarts. What should you recommend?
opts: Move the orchestrator to a Premium plan
Store the time in a static variable
Increase the function timeout to unbounded
Use the orchestration context's current time and GUID APIs, because orchestrators replay and must be deterministic
questions.e: Orchestrators rebuild state by replaying history, so non-deterministic calls must use context APIs or move to activities.

questions.q: A company runs microservices in an Azure Container Apps environment with Dapr. It wants event-driven functions with triggers and bindings in the same environment, sharing its network and logs. What should you recommend?
opts: A separate Flex Consumption app integrated with the same VNet
Deploy the functions as Azure Functions on Azure Container Apps in that environment
Logic Apps Consumption workflows
A Premium plan app with Hybrid Connections

questions.q: Evaluate these statements about the Flex Consumption plan. 1: It supports virtual network integration. 2: It supports deployment slots. 3: It supports custom container images. 4: It runs only on Linux. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 4 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only

questions.q: Dozens of workflows each run thousands of actions every hour, 24 hours a day. The company wants predictable cost and private networking. What should you recommend?
opts: Logic Apps Standard on a Workflow Standard hosting plan
Azure Functions Consumption plan on Windows
Logic Apps Consumption with an integration account
Logic Apps Consumption with fewer retries

questions.q: A function app needs inbound private endpoints and outbound VNet integration. Which hosting option should you NOT recommend?
opts: Dedicated plan
Premium plan
Consumption plan
Flex Consumption plan
questions.e: The legacy Consumption plan supports neither inbound private endpoints nor VNet integration.

questions.q: A booking saga calls four services and must run compensation steps if any call fails. Developers want the logic in C#, with unit tests and source control, and durable state across restarts. What should you recommend?
opts: An Azure Container Apps job per booking
A Durable Functions orchestration with compensation logic
Four independent HTTP functions that call each other
A Logic Apps Consumption workflow designed in the portal

questions.q: An operations team with no developers needs a workflow that sends an approval email through Office 365, waits several days for a response and then updates a SharePoint list. What should you recommend?
opts: A stateless Logic Apps Standard workflow
A timer-triggered function on the Flex Consumption plan
A Durable Functions human interaction orchestration
A stateful Logic Apps workflow using the Office 365 approval action

questions.q: A regulated workload requires function apps on fully isolated single-tenant compute and network, with very high scale and fixed infrastructure cost. What should you recommend?
opts: A Premium plan with private endpoints
Azure Functions on Container Apps with a Consumption profile
A Dedicated plan in an App Service Environment v3
A Flex Consumption plan with VNet integration

questions.q: A partner allows calls only from a known static public IP. A serverless function app must call the partner while keeping pay-per-use billing. What should you recommend?
opts: Flex Consumption with a private endpoint for inbound traffic
Consumption plan with its shared outbound IP addresses
Premium plan with Hybrid Connections
Flex Consumption with VNet integration and a NAT gateway on the integration subnet
questions.e: Outbound traffic through VNet integration can leave via a NAT gateway with a fixed public IP.

questions.q: Security requires that a function app's triggers and bindings to Storage and Service Bus use no connection strings or keys. What should you recommend?
opts: Identity-based connections using the app's managed identity with RBAC roles
Shared access signatures renewed by a timer function
Connection strings stored in app settings
Connection strings stored as Key Vault references

questions.q: Evaluate these statements about Logic Apps Standard. 1: It supports both stateful and stateless workflows. 2: It is billed per action execution like Consumption. 3: Workflows can be developed and run locally in Visual Studio Code. Which statements are true?
opts: Statement 1 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3
Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1 and 3 only

questions.q: A thumbnail function needs native image libraries packaged in a custom Linux container. It must scale to zero when idle and minimise cost. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Functions Premium plan with one always-ready instance
Azure Functions Dedicated plan with Always On
Azure Functions on Azure Container Apps with minimum replicas set to zero
Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan
questions.e: Flex Consumption doesn't support containers, and Premium keeps at least one instance warm and billed.

questions.q: A containerized HTTP microservice gets traffic only during business events, must scale to zero, use Dapr pub/sub and have a custom domain with a managed certificate. What should you recommend?
opts: Azure Container Apps on the Consumption profile
Azure App Service for Containers on a Basic plan
Azure Container Instances with a public IP
Azure Kubernetes Service with the cluster autoscaler

questions.q: In one function app, a busy queue-triggered function competes for instances with latency-sensitive HTTP functions, and HTTP response times suffer during queue spikes. The team wants serverless billing and one app. What should you recommend?
opts: Add a deployment slot for the queue function
Move the app to the Consumption plan and raise the instance limit
Host the app on Flex Consumption, where non-HTTP triggers scale on their own instances
Move the app to a Dedicated plan with manual scale
questions.e: Flex Consumption uses per-function scaling: HTTP triggers scale together, while other trigger types such as queues scale independently.
